title: Tourism puts Zanzibari reserve at a crossroads | Science
content: The moist broadleaf forests located on the coasts of Tanzania and Kenya and on nearby archipelagos such as Zanzibar are highly fragmented hotspots of plant and animal diversity (1). On Pemba, the 988-km2 northernmost island of Zanzibar, the largest remaining forest and principal protected area is the 14.4-km2 Ngezi-Vumawimbi Nature Forest Reserve. The forest’s integrity is imminently threatened by the development of Mantuli Luxury Estate, a resort set to convert an estimated 17% of the forest reserve into a sprawling complex of villas and swimming pools (2). Zanzibar should reconsider the location of the resort to protect its vulnerable forests.
